fields.statement: QA at e6c86be2 with a built binary (go build ./cmd/rhiza): from a subfolder of a scratch dir outside any root, rhiza root show exits 2 'not inside a Rhiza root'; after rhiza root init on the parent, root show from the subfolder (text and --json) names the parent as root; from this checkout it names /home/rhiza/code, project rhiza: the CLI still resolves the root from its absolute cwd. go test -trimpath ./internal/rootcfg/... and ./internal/api/... -run Usage pass (TestFindEmptyDirFindsNoRoot, TestUsageLearnEmptyWdStaysInRepoFolder). In a git-archive copy under a scratch root with rootcfg.go reverted to 2a7a01a1^, the usage tests fail and a fake hit (hit_at 2026-11-04T10:45Z) lands in the scratch root's .rhiza-root/usage.limits.jsonl; with the fix restored they pass and no .rhiza-root is created.

QA at e6c86be2: go test -trimpath ./internal/rootguard/... passes. From this checkout under the real root ~/code, ./internal/api/... -run Usage, the full ./internal/api/... and ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/usage ran with a before/after snapshot of ~/code/.rhiza-root (file list, sizes, mtimes, limits file hash): identical, nothing written. Negative check: in a copy under a scratch root with the rootcfg fix reverted, rootguard.Main in api's TestMain failed the run with '.rhiza-root/usage.limits.jsonl: line 1 appended with hit_at 2026-11-04T10:45:00Z, outside the test run'. The full api run had one unrelated failure, TestWebRootHandlerServesEveryProject's TempDir cleanup ('directory not empty'), which passes 3/3 alone and is in code this change does not touch.
